utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm the doctor today. I hear you've had burning when you wee since yesterday. Tell me a bit more about it — how often are you going, is there any blood in the urine, and does it feel like you can't fully empty?
reply: It stings and burns, and it is the worst right at the end. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out and I have to rush. It started yesterday morning, and the urine is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

I am eating normally and haven't been sick, and I don't think I could be pregnant because my last period was about two weeks ago and it was normal, plus I am on the pill and I don't miss it.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: Your urine test strip shows signs of infection, and with your symptoms and no fever or back pain, this looks like a simple bladder infection (cystitis). One other thing I'd suggest: because you're under 30, sexually active without condoms and have never had a sexual health check, it's recommended to do a chlamydia and gonorrhoea test — it's just done on the same urine sample, and chlamydia often has no symptoms but can occasionally cause burning like this. Are you happy for me to add that?
reply: Oh right, okay, we can do that. Can I just get the script for the antibiotics now so I can get back to work?

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Here's your script: trimethoprim 300 mg, one tablet at night for 3 days — that's the standard first-choice treatment in Australia for a bladder infection, and it won't interfere with your pill. You should feel noticeably better within 1–2 days, but please finish all three tablets. A few other things:

- Drink plenty of water today and over the next few days, and cut back on the coffee while you're unwell. You can take paracetamol for the discomfort if needed; Ural sachets can ease the sting but don't take them at the same time as the trimethoprim.
- Try to wee after sex and don't hold on when you need to go — this helps prevent repeat infections.
- Please come back urgently, or go to the emergency department after hours, if you develop fever, shivers or shakes, pain in your back or sides, vomiting, you see blood in your urine, or if you're not improving after 2 days or getting worse — that could mean the infection has spread to the kidneys and needs different treatment.
- If it comes back again soon after finishing the antibiotics, come back and we'll send a urine sample to the lab to check for a resistant bug.
- We'll have the chlamydia/gonorrhoea result in about 2 days; we'll contact you if it's positive, and if it's negative you can assume no news is good news, or ring to check. Does that all make sense, and any questions?
reply: That all makes sense, thank you. I'll get these tablets picked up and head back to the cafe now.
